summary: Over two iterations, we improved the Traveling Santa score from ~69.5 (iter-1) to a median of ~78.8 (iter-2) by implementing grid-guided 2-opt with penalty-aware fast delta computation, Or-opt moves, and simulated annealing. Double-bridge perturbation was tested and found to hurt performance within the 2-second time limit — continuous SA without perturbation is strictly better (median 78.83 vs 78.68).
key_points: Best reliable score is ~78.8 (median across runs), achieved by continuous SA with grid-guided 2-opt, penalty-aware delta, Or-opt, and position tracking. Score variance of ±5 points is caused by machine load against the 2s time limit.

Double-bridge perturbation (ILS pattern) was REFUTED as an improvement: the O(N) tour cost recompute after perturbation plus SA restart overhead exceeds the diversification benefit at N=200K in 2 seconds.

The iter-2 handoff incorrectly stated iter-1 scored 78.9 — actual iter-1 score was 69.5. Both iter-2 arms beat this substantially (~+9 points), confirming the grid-guided neighbor selection and penalty-aware delta are the dominant improvements.

Next iteration should focus on: (1) reducing score variance by optimizing time management (adaptive iteration counts based on N), (2) trying LK-style 3-opt or larger Or-opt segments (2-3 cities) which iter-2 coded but may not have fully exploited, (3) smarter prime scheduling — currently a post-pass, but integrating prime-awareness into the SA acceptance criterion could yield better penalty avoidance, (4) better initial construction (e.g., greedy nearest-neighbor with penalty awareness instead of grid-NN).

Key unknown: whether the ~78.8 ceiling is from the algorithm quality or from time pressure. If we can do 2x more SA iterations per second (e.g., via cache-friendly tour representation, or SIMD distance computation), the score could jump significantly.
